name: Temples (Insula XXX)
period: late 3rd century AD (c. 270–280): the large and small Romano-Celtic temples of Insula XXX as planned in 1890 (Fox & St John Hope; east halves completed on plan), in their walled precinct; the north temple (demolished c. AD 200) left out

frame.note: local u (east-ish), v (north-ish) metres; E,N = origin + R(angle)*(u,v); the frame is square to the large temple (-4.3 deg from grid north), origin the in-rings' SW bounding corner. Walls fitted to the Great Plan rings (tmp/key-plans/temples-scripts/fitwalls.py).

conventions: walls: centreline a->b, thickness t, height h; openings at metres from a, width w, height oh. conjecture:true marks things not evidenced.

rooms.name: Ambulatory (east, front)
rooms.note: ambulatory floor: "a pavement of common opus signinum 2 inches thick, made of coarsely-pounded brick embedded in hard white cement", laid "at a height of 7½ feet above the original ground level" on a fill of sandy clay and loam (Fox & St John Hope 1890, p. 746)

rooms.name: Cella of the large temple
rooms.note: cella floor at the same level: opus signinum about 5 inches thick, its upper layer of brick fragments "mixed with pieces of hard stone, the most conspicuous being a streaked limestone of a dark colour, seemingly from the Purbeck beds", "ground down level and then smoothed and polished" (Fox & St John Hope 1890, p. 746)

lining.note: Purbeck marble wall-linings ("from their thinness ... evidently wall-linings") and "mouldings of plaster panels covered with a fine white stucco" found near both temples (Fox & St John Hope 1890, p. 747): material S; where they were (a dado of slabs to 1 m, framed panels above, a thin red line in each panel) X

Shown up to the floor, 7½ ft (2.3 m), with the colonnade on it

columns.note: peristyle round the cella on the podium wall, as Fox read the large temple ("sufficiently broad to have carried columns"); no column, base or capital was found, so the diameter is about the forum colonnade's (0.57 m, Fox & St John Hope 1893), the height 7 diameters, Vitruvius's Tuscan rule ("the thickness of the columns at the bottom be one seventh of their height", IV.7), with timber main beams as he gives them; 8 bays a side, the middle bay on the east left open for the steps

stairs.note: steps up to the podium, 2.3 m: none found; nine steps on the east, between the middle columns (conjecture; Fulford 2002's reconstruction of a Romano-Celtic temple has its steps on the entrance side)
steps up to the small temple's door: none found; five steps, the top ones in the doorway (conjecture)

fittings.note: cult statue on a pedestal, against the back wall on the axis, facing the door: no base or statue was found in either cella (Fox & St John Hope 1890); the cella housed the god's image (Historic England 2018), as at Uley, where Mercury's limestone statue, "a little larger than life-size (approximately 2m.)", stood on a base (British Museum 1978,0102.1); Vitruvius IV.5 turns the statue to face as the temple does. The deity is unknown (Fulford et al. 2017 for the north temple): a plain draped figure with an offering dish, no attributes (X). Pedestal faced with Purbeck marble, as the linings found here; its panel's text is not known

offering table before the statue, with two small terracotta lamps and a dish: "two small lamps of terra-cotta" were found at the temples (Fox & St John Hope 1890, p. 747); the table and where the lamps stood are conjecture

inscribed Purbeck marble dedication panel: thin (19 mm) Purbeck slabs with dedications by the guild of peregrini were found "in the shrine" of the Romano-Celtic temple in Insula XXXV (RIB 69-71); none from these temples, so their place and text here are conjecture
